recruit.eyebrow: FIND THE PEOPLE YOUR BOARD NEEDS
recruit.headline: Prepare a board recruitment campaign you can carry out yourself.
recruit.intro: Your next board member should bring something your organization needs. Start with your mission, the people already around your board table and the work ahead. Then prepare a clear opportunity and give suitable people a practical way to apply.
recruit.hero_note: Learn the process and share your starting information before you decide to purchase.
recruit.education_eyebrow: HOW TO CARRY OUT THE PROCESS
recruit.education_heading: What you and your organization will do
teaching: Decide who belongs around your board table

Look at the experience, relationships and capabilities your board already has. Identify the gaps that matter to your mission and describe the contribution you want a new member to make. A useful profile is about the work someone can help you accomplish.
Make the opportunity clear

Explain your mission, the responsibilities of serving on your board and the time you expect members to contribute. Prepare your organization overview, agreements and recruitment announcement before you invite people to consider the role.
Launch and promote your campaign

Approve your public materials and confirm your launch. Your application form becomes active, and the platform reports the outcome of marketplace publication and eligible network notifications. Use your approved posts and application link on LinkedIn, Facebook, your website and through personal outreach.
Review applications and have meaningful interviews

Read what each applicant has actually shared, including their supporting documents. Prepare questions about their experience, motivation, availability and expectations. You make the selection decisions and use the reference, appointment and onboarding templates when appropriate.
recruit.service_heading: Get the tools and carry out the work yourself.
recruit.outcome: We provide your customized recruitment pack, the application system and practical interview tools. You review the materials, confirm the campaign launch, promote the opportunity and decide whom to appoint.
recruit.service_body: You can follow this process without necessarily spending thousands of dollars on consultants. The self-service service costs $197 for this product. If you want us to work with you or provide more direct help, book a conversation and we will discuss a separate quotation.
recruit.closing_heading: Start with what you know about your organization.
recruit.closing_body: The free questions help us understand your situation. You will then see exactly what happens next and what your purchase includes.

board-fundraising-game.headline: Bring your board's fundraising ideas into one agreed strategy.
board-fundraising-game.intro: People around your organization often know different audiences, businesses and grantmakers that may have good reasons to support your mission. Give each person room to develop their thinking before the meeting, then agree together which opportunities you will pursue.
board-fundraising-game.hero_note: Learn the process and share your starting information before you decide to purchase.
board-fundraising-game.education_eyebrow: HOW TO CARRY OUT THE PROCESS
board-fundraising-game.education_heading: What you and your organization will do
teaching: Start with a clear fundraising goal

Explain what your organization needs to fund and why it matters. Invite board members, staff and volunteers who can contribute useful knowledge. They do not need to arrive with every answer or invent an opportunity to take part.
Develop one funding audience at a time

Each person considers individuals, businesses and grantmakers. For each audience they identify, ask why it may give, where to find it, how to attract its interest and how to build a relationship. Then discuss what to ask it to support and an appropriate amount. A participant can add another audience or move to the next category.
Compare the ideas during your next meeting

Read the contributions in advance and use the facilitation guide to introduce the discussion. During the Group Game, compare overlapping suggestions without losing different approaches. Edit or combine ideas, add an idea agreed during discussion and explicitly adopt the ones your group wants to pursue.
Agree how people will participate

After discussing the audiences, review what each person is willing to contribute. Record responsibilities only when the person agrees. Review and approve the final strategy, including the approved audiences and confirmed participation commitments, then begin carrying out the work.

strategic-planning.eyebrow: DEVELOP YOUR PLAN WITH YOUR BOARD
strategic-planning.headline: Guide your board toward a strategic plan it understands and approves.
strategic-planning.intro: A useful strategic plan starts with your organization's present reality. Share what you know, invite your board's thinking and make time to discuss the decisions together. You can facilitate that process yourself with clear questions and practical guidance.
strategic-planning.hero_note: Learn the process and share your starting information before you decide to purchase.
strategic-planning.education_eyebrow: HOW TO CARRY OUT THE PROCESS
strategic-planning.education_heading: What you and your organization will do
teaching: Prepare a truthful starting point

Bring your mission, goals, objectives, programs and current needs into the conversation. Describe your team, technology, marketing, partnerships and fundraising. Include budget figures you actually know and say where information is still uncertain.
Ask board members to contribute before the meeting

Give each person the planning form and enough time to reflect. Preserve their individual ideas so you can see where perspectives agree and where discussion is needed. Review the responses before the meeting rather than starting with a blank page.
Discuss priorities and make clear decisions

Use the facilitation guide and group session to work through the existing planning topics. Compare proposals, edit or combine ideas and confirm the decisions your board adopts. You can retain your current mission. A suggestion stays a suggestion until you confirm it.
Review and approve the plan

Bring the adopted decisions into a consolidated preview. Check the wording and include budget or fundraising components where your group supplied the necessary figures. Approve the final plan, distribute it to your board and use it to guide your organization's work.

board-recommitment.eyebrow: HAVE THE RIGHT CONVERSATION WITH YOUR BOARD
board-recommitment.headline: Find out how your board members are willing to contribute moving forward.
board-recommitment.intro: When expectations or circumstances change, give each board member a respectful opportunity to reflect. Explain why you need the board to recommit, ask what each person can offer and use their response to prepare a meaningful conversation.
board-recommitment.hero_note: Learn the process and share your starting information before you decide to purchase.
board-recommitment.education_eyebrow: HOW TO CARRY OUT THE PROCESS
board-recommitment.education_heading: What you and your organization will do
teaching: Clarify what you need from your board

Explain your mission, why recommitment matters now and what you need members to help accomplish. Be clear about the relevant deadline and expectations. Members can give more useful answers when they understand the work ahead.
Invite a considered response

Send each person the recommitment invitation and form link. You can use your own email account or the platform's authorized sending option. Give people time to reflect and use the two respectful follow-up templates when someone has not responded.
Read what the person actually said

Look for willingness, concerns, capacity and expectations in the response. A submitted form does not automatically mean someone has recommitted. Where their meaning is uncertain, prepare a question rather than assuming an intention.
Prepare and conduct the follow-up conversation

Generate a personalized conversation guide, edit it and approve the version you want to use. Receive the guide by email and talk with the board member independently. Your organization makes the decisions about continued service and next steps.
